hero.title: The Shishunaga Dynasty: Magadhan Consolidation
hero.description: A pivotal era in Ancient Indian history marking the transition from Haryanka to the Nanda hegemony, focusing on the strategic shift of power to Pataliputra.

timeline.title: The Chronological Framework
timeline.description: Chronological milestones of the Shishunaga Dynasty.

cards.details: Shishunaga deposes the Haryanka ruler Nagadashaka, ending the dynasty and establishing the Shishunaga line.
Accession of Kalashoka (Kakavarna), who formally shifted the capital from Vaishali to Pataliputra.
The Second Buddhist Council held at Vaishali under the royal patronage of Kalashoka.

items.decryption: Remember the sequence of primary Shishunaga rulers: Shishunaga (Founder), Kalashoka (Council), and the transition to Nandas.

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Confusing the Second Buddhist Council location: It was held at Vaishali, not Pataliputra (which hosted the 3rd).
Assuming Bimbisara belonged to the Shishunaga dynasty; he was Haryanka.
Mistaking the shift of capital: Shishunaga moved it to Vaishali, Kalashoka moved it back to Pataliputra.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Geography

  • Centered in Magadha (Bihar).
  • Strategic control over the Ganges-Son-Gandak river network.
  • Access to iron ore mines of Rajgir.

Personalities

  • Shishunaga: Founder, defeated Avanti.
  • Kalashoka: Patronized 2nd Buddhist Council.

Core Evolution: Magadhan Expansion

  • The Avanti Rivalry: Shishunaga’s greatest achievement was the annexation of Avanti, effectively ending the long-standing rivalry between Magadha and Ujjain.
  • Administrative Shift: The transition from the 'Father-Son' murder cycle (Haryanka) to a more systemic, albeit brief, political stability.
  • Second Buddhist Council: A crucial religious milestone reflecting the royal involvement in the sectarian divisions (Sthaviras vs Mahasanghikas).
RulerKey Achievement
ShishunagaDefeated the Pradyota dynasty of Avanti.
KalashokaShifted capital to Pataliputra permanently.
